title: Grateful Dead Live at Boston Music Hall on 1971-04-08

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard captures a smoking Bertha and a fiery Truckin' with standout rhythm guitar, despite slightly back vocals.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised as one of the juiciest sources available – a soundboard mix where guitars are crystal clear, bass solid and the overall balance near perfect, though vocals sit a bit low. Musically the show shines on Bertha, which reviewers call “SMOKIN,” and an unexpectedly powerful Truckin' that highlights Bob Weir’s rhythm work, even if Jerry Garcia’s lead is less prominent. Overall the energy feels high and the mix, while occasionally harsh on the guitar, remains very listenable.

ai_rating.rationale: Both reviewers give high marks (5 and 4 stars) and highlight strong performances and a high‑quality soundboard recording, with only minor mix quirks.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Guitars crystal clear, bass solid, vocals slightly recessed; Bob Weir's rhythm guitar is very forward – sometimes harsh – but adds excitement. Overall mix described as near perfect.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Limited detail, but reviewers note a consistently high‑energy performance with strong highlights in the second half.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Not prominently heard on this recording; described as “nowhere to be found.”
band_member_comments.Bob: Rhythm guitar front‑and‑center with vivid picks and fret slides; at times too loud/harsh but adds excitement.
